newsitem.title: USA: Yellow sees more cost savings in '97.
newsitem.headline: Yellow sees more cost savings in '97.

text.p: Yellow Corp, which provides less-than-truckload service, said in its 1996 annual report that it will implement the second phase of cost reduction initiatives in 1997. No details were provided.

It said cost cutting moves, implemented in late 1995, helped the company achieve targeted savings of $75 million in 1996 and are expected to have a full-year impact this year with expected savings exceeding $90 million.
Last year, Yellow restructured itself and decentralized into five business units.
In connection with some of the changes for 1997, as reported on March 6, Yellow said it intends to increase its use of intermodal rail service to move freight.

Yellow projects 1997 net capital expenditures will total $109 million, compared to $46 million in 1996, chairman A. Maurice Myers said in his letter to shareholders. This investment will be focused on the replacement of tractor and trailer equipment and on attaining improved operating efficiencies, he noted.
